question: The marked price of a jacket is Rs. 3,500. A shopkeeper offers 5% discount on it and then again offers 15% discount on the new price, and then again offers 20% discount on the new price. How much one has to pay for it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply successive discounts directly using fraction multipliers:

SP = 3500 × 95% × 85% × 80%

SP = 3500 × 19/20 × 17/20 × 4/5

SP = (3500 ÷ 2000) × 19 × 17 × 4

SP = 7/4 × 1292 = 2261

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,261.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of jacket = Rs. 3,500

Successive discounts = 5%, 15%, and 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100 × (100 − d₃)/100

 MP
 
 3500

 
•

 3325

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 3500 × (100 − 5)/100 × (100 − 15)/100 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ SP = 3500 × 95/100 × 85/100 × 80/100

⇒ SP = 3500 × 19/20 × 17/20 × 4/5

⇒ SP = 3500 × (19 × 17 × 4) ÷ (20 × 20 × 5)

⇒ SP = 3500 × 1292 ÷ 2000

⇒ SP = (3500 ÷ 2000) × 1292

⇒ SP = 7/4 × 1292

⇒ SP = 7 × 323 = 2261

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,261.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The marked price is the regular price tag printed on an item. Any discount given by a shopkeeper is always calculated on the MP, not the cost price.

Successive Discount Formula

When an article has multiple consecutive discounts, the net selling price is derived by multiplying the individual discount factors: SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × ...

Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the effective single discount equivalent to both combined is calculated using the net change formula: (x + y − xy/100)%.
